name: navigation
display_name: Navigate to a named waypoint (EasyNav-backed, real navigation)
description: Moves the robot to one of a fixed set of named waypoints (configured on this node as ROS parameters) by driving a real EasyNav navigation stack through easynav::GoalManagerClient. Internally structured as a BehaviorTree.CPP tree (StartOff -> Navigate -> Finish). Unlike a mock navigation capability, this is a real easyfleet_core::NavigationActionServerBase backend -- see easyfleet_easynav_navigation.

action.name: /robot_1/navigation or /robot_2/navigation, depending on which robot announced it

goal.parameters_json: string - REQUIRED for this backend: a JSON object with a string field "goal_id" naming one of the waypoints configured on this node (see 'parameters' below for the current list). Goals without a valid goal_id are rejected.

feedback.current_pose: geometry_msgs/PoseStamped - robot's current pose, as reported by EasyNav.
feedback.navigation_time: builtin_interfaces/Duration - time elapsed since this navigation goal started, as reported by EasyNav.
feedback.distance_remaining: float32 - straight-line distance left to the goal, as reported by EasyNav.
feedback.number_of_recoveries: int16 - always 0: EasyNav has no equivalent concept.
feedback.current_waypoint_index: uint32 - always 0: this backend navigates to one waypoint per goal, not a waypoint list.

result.error_code: uint16 - 0 SUCCESS, 1 REJECTED, 2 ABORTED, 3 CANCELED, 4 TIMEOUT, 10 NO_PATH_FOUND, 11 LOCALIZATION_LOST.
result.error_msg: string - human-readable explanation, populated when error_code is non-zero.
result.final_pose: geometry_msgs/PoseStamped - robot's pose when the goal ended, as reported by EasyNav.
result.total_time: builtin_interfaces/Duration - not populated by this backend (left at its default).

requirements: parameters_json must contain a "goal_id" naming one of this node's configured waypoints.

EasyNav (easynav_system system_main) must already be running and reachable on the easynav_control topic, localized on the home2 map, with this robot's Gazebo instance publishing scan_raw and the TF tree the costmap localizer/controller expect.
effects: On success (error_code == SUCCESS), the robot's physical location changes to be at (or very near) the requested waypoint.
A currently executing goal can be preempted by a newer navigation goal: EasyNav is redirected to the new waypoint without stopping first (see 'preemption' below).
A canceled or capability-shutdown goal sends EasyNav an explicit cancellation, stopping the robot.

preemption.behavior_when_enabled: Sending a new goal while one is active aborts the previous ROS goal, but EasyNav itself is redirected (not stopped) to the new waypoint -- the robot keeps moving, just towards the new target.
preemption.behavior_when_disabled: Sending a new goal while one is active is rejected outright; the caller must wait for the current navigation to finish, or explicitly cancel it, before sending another.

navigation.allow_preemption.description: Whether a new navigation goal is allowed to preempt (replace) one that is currently executing.

navigation.tick_rate_hz.description: Rate at which the internal behavior tree is ticked while a goal is executing.

navigation.waypoint_ids.description: The set of named waypoints this node accepts as parameters_json.goal_id, valid on the home2 map (see navigation_params.yaml). Each id must have a matching navigation.waypoints.<id>.{frame_id,x,y,yaw} sub-parameter.

capabilities_file.description: Path to this very capability description file; published verbatim on /capabilities when the node is activated.

behavior_tree_xml.description: Path to the BehaviorTree.CPP XML tree to run per goal (StartOff -> Navigate -> Finish, reused from easyfleet_easynav_deployment).

bt_plugins.description: Paths to the BT.CPP plugin shared libraries (BT_REGISTER_NODES) to load before building the tree -- every node the tree XML references must come from one of these. Reused directly from easyfleet_easynav_deployment (libstart_off_bt_node.so/libfinish_bt_node.so) and easyfleet_easynav_navigation (libeasynav_navigate_bt_node.so); this package supplies no BT plugins of its own.

notes: This backend drives a real EasyNav navigation stack (easynav_system system_main) with a real navigation configuration -- see config/robot_1|robot_2/easynav_system.costmap_rpp.params.yaml (AMCLLocalizer + CostmapMapsManager + RegulatedPurePursuitController, copied from src/easynav_indoor_testcase/robots_params/costmap.rpp.params.yaml). Goals actually complete once the robot reaches the waypoint (within system_node's position_tolerance/angle_tolerance).

Deployment: the two-robot 'easynav_collaboration' scenario -- system_main and this capability are namespaced under /robot_1 and /robot_2 respectively (each its own process, its own launch/robot_N_launch.yaml), on the same shared home2 map. system_main's own 'tf_prefix' parameter is set to match, so TF/goal frames stay consistent per robot -- see easyfleet_easynav_deployment's README section on tf_prefix for the full explanation.

The executable itself (easynav_navigation_capability_node) is not duplicated in this package: it is reused directly from easyfleet_easynav_deployment, launched twice (once per robot) with different namespaces/parameters.
